title: Knowledge Check 8 - Lessons 36-40
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 36-40 - AI Agents. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A customer-service agent that works well in live chat is connected to email and starts failing. What is the most likely reason?
options: Email requires a different agent type
Email is turn-based with no live session, so conversation variables the agent expects are not carried across messages
Email cannot reach the agent at all
The agent needs more standard actions
questions.explanation: Email runs through Email-to-Case as a turn-based interaction without a persistent session, so an agent that assumes a live chat session loses the state it depends on.

questions.question: On a messaging surface, what determines whose data access the service agent uses by default?
options: The customer's browser permissions
The signed-in site user automatically
The dedicated agent user, unless credential-based verification is enabled
The Slack workspace owner
questions.explanation: A service agent typically runs as a dedicated agent user, and only credential-based verification switches it to run as the signed-in site user.

questions.question: An action returns a rich choice picker, but the channel does not declare that format. What happens?
options: The platform converts it to plain text automatically
The agent rebuilds the action for that channel
The channel silently upgrades itself
The response renders poorly or not at all, because the channel does not support that adaptive response format
questions.explanation: Adaptive response formats are declared per connection, so a format the channel does not carry produces a degraded or empty result rather than a graceful conversion.

questions.question: A service agent cannot retrieve a record it is supposed to know about, even though the action is configured correctly. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Trust Layer is blocking the record
The agent's running user, the agent user, lacks access to the record through permissions or sharing
The topic instructions are too short
The channel does not support rich responses
questions.explanation: The agent acts under its running user, so a missing object or field permission or a sharing gap on the agent user blocks the record before the action can return it.

questions.question: How does the Einstein Trust Layer relate to which records an agent can read?
options: It grants the agent access to any record it needs
It replaces sharing rules for agents
It governs model traffic, such as injection filtering and toxicity checks, not record access, which the running user enforces
It stores agent data in a separate store
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer operates between the agent and the model with content and audit controls; record-level access stays with the running user's permissions and sharing.

questions.question: An employee agent runs in the Agentforce panel. Whose permissions determine what it can reach?
options: The signed-in user's profile, permissions, field-level security, and sharing
A shared administrator identity
The Trust Layer defaults
The channel's response formats
questions.explanation: An employee agent runs as the logged-in user, so that person's access controls govern what the agent can query, modify, and do.

questions.question: An action passes in the builder but fails for a customer in production. What is the most useful first step?
options: Rewrite the topic instructions
Add more actions to the topic
Check the running user's permissions and the action's run context, since the builder ran under your identity and production runs under the agent user
Change the channel's response format
questions.explanation: The builder runs under the admin identity while production runs as the agent user or the employee, so the recovery starts by checking the running user's access and the action's execution context.

questions.question: A Flow action reaches records the running user should not be able to see. What most likely explains it?
options: The Trust Layer widened access
The Flow runs in system context or the Apex runs without sharing, so it can reach beyond the running user's access
The agent has too many topics
The channel is unauthenticated
questions.explanation: A Flow in system context or Apex without sharing can exceed the running user's reach, which is exactly why the action's execution context must be reviewed alongside the running user.

questions.question: Which statement about the Einstein Trust Layer for agents is correct?
options: It enforces record-level sharing for the agent
It replaces the need for least privilege on the agent user
Its data masking is applied to every agent response by default
It governs model traffic with injection filtering, toxicity checks, and audit logging, and record access stays with the running user
questions.explanation: The Trust Layer operates at inference time on model traffic, and because its data masking is not applied for agents, record-level access remains the running user's responsibility.

questions.question: A company wants an agent that answers benefits and IT policy questions for its own staff inside the Salesforce app. Which agent type fits?
options: A Service agent on Enhanced Chat
An Employee agent, because it serves internal users and runs in the logged-in user context
A Lead Nurturing agent sending email
A public Service agent on the marketing site
questions.explanation: The audience is internal staff on an internal channel, which is exactly what an Employee agent serves, and it runs as the logged-in user. A Service agent targets external customers.

questions.question: A retailer wants an agent on its public website where anonymous shoppers ask about returns, and signed-in shoppers must see only their own orders. What does the consultant build?
options: A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel, with credential-based user verification so signed-in shoppers run as their own site user
An Employee agent assigned to each shopper
A Lead Nurturing agent
An Employee agent deployed in Slack
questions.explanation: External website shoppers belong to a Service agent, and credential-based verification is the mechanism that makes a signed-in shopper run as their own site user so they see only their own orders.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how the two agent types differ at run time?
options: Employee agents run as the agent user and Service agents as the logged-in user
Both always run as guest users
Employee agents run as the logged-in user while Service agents run as a dedicated agent user unless credential-based verification applies
Neither inherits Salesforce sharing rules
questions.explanation: The Employee agent runs as the logged-in end user and the Service agent runs as its Agent User, with the verified site user taking over only when credential-based verification applies.

questions.question: A service team wants an agent that handles customer chats on the company website and hands hard cases to a human agent. Which type and running identity fit?
options: An Employee agent running as the logged-in rep
A Lead Nurturing agent sending email
A Service agent on an enhanced messaging channel, running as the Agent User and escalating to a human when the case is complex
A retired Agentforce (Default) agent
questions.explanation: External customer chats arrive with no Salesforce login, so a Service agent runs as the Agent User and hands complicated cases to a human. An Employee agent would require the caller to be an authenticated internal user.

questions.question: An anonymous shopper chats on a website and then logs in mid conversation, after which they must see only their own orders. What makes that possible?
options: Setting a context variable with the shopper's email
A context variable identifies the user but does not control access, so credential-based verification switches the session to the verified site user whose sharing rules limit the data
Assigning the shopper to a profile by hand
Nothing, because a Service agent always sees all orders
questions.explanation: Context tells the agent who the person claims to be, but access is governed by the running identity, which only switches to the verified site user once credential-based verification succeeds.

questions.question: A company needs both an internal help agent and a customer-facing agent. What is the correct design?
options: One agent with every subagent attached so it can answer anything
Split the two audiences across two agents with non-overlapping subagents and action lists
One Employee agent placed on the public site for both audiences
One Service agent assigned to internal staff
questions.explanation: The running user differs between the two audiences, so you stand up two agents with disjoint subagents rather than one agent trying to act as both an internal person and an external visitor.
